newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka '97 economic growth seen at six percent.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka '97 economic growth seen at six percent.

text.p: Sri Lanka's economic growth in 1997 is seen touching six percent against 3.8 percent in the previous year mainly due to lower interest rates, the Central Bank governor said on Friday.
"We are reasonably optimistic of achieving an overall growth rate of six percent this year," Amarananda Jayawardena told Reuters in an interview on Friday.
He said the economic growth momentum witnessed in the first half was likely to be sustained as the energy sector and agriculture were performing better.
Industrial production is also seen up as companies, which held on to their investment plans last year due to high interest rates, were implementing them this year, he said.
The Central Bank reduced reserve ratios for banks earlier this year, creating more liquidity in the market that brought interest rates down.
Prime lending rates were down to an average of 14.7 percent in the week ending June 19 from 17.2 percent in the same period last year, the Central Bank said.
